title: Traffic spike on a stateless API
story: 60 users (1 s think time) flood one web replica capped at 0.5 CPU (about 25 req/s). Expected heal: scale out.

timeline.thought: Dry run passed with no guardrail violations. Proceeding to apply.

args.summary: Scaled stateless web service from 1 to 3 replicas to relieve CPU saturation (peak 52.9% against the 50%-per-replica cpu limit) causing request queuing/timeouts and the 1489-1800ms latency spikes.

timeline.thought:
ROOT CAUSE: CPU saturation on the single `web` replica — probe latency stepped from a steady ~22-24ms baseline to 1800ms/1489ms/1716ms/1571ms (threshold 800ms) right as `cpu_pct_peak_total` hit 52.9% against the 50%-per-replica cpu limit (`cpus: 0.5`), with a resulting client-side timeout/BrokenPipeError in the logs — classic symptom of each CPU-bound request (~20ms CPU each) queuing up once the single replica's CPU budget was exhausted, not a code or dependency fault (mem usage was only 20.8MB/128MB, no OOM, no restarts/exit codes).

CHANGE: Scaled the stateless `web` service from 1 to 3 replicas (memory/cpus per replica unchanged) so traefik can load-balance CPU-bound requests across more CPU budget instead of raising the per-replica cpu limit.

GUARDRAILS: Within policy — replicas 3 ≤ max_replicas 3, allowed_actions includes "scale", service marked stateless, total memory 3×128MiB=384MiB ≤ max_total_memory 768m, per-replica cpus unchanged at 0.5 ≤ max_cpus 1.0; dry-run validate returned ok with no violations.

FOLLOW-UP: Monitor WatchDock's automatic 5-consecutive-probe verification over the next 60s; if latency doesn't recover, consider also raising per-replica cpus toward 1.0 or review if traffic bursts regularly exceed 3-replica capacity, which would need a capacity-planning (non-automated) decision.
